mechanism_narrative: A lower level of the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is causally linked to higher S&P 500 forward 5-day returns because it reduces the cost of capital for corporations and encourages risk-taking in equity markets.
failure_condition: The Rank IC between FEDFUNDS and 5-day SPX returns is greater than or equal to -0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate above 4.5% signals a restrictive monetary policy that increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5%, or the Rank IC between FEDFUNDS (above 4.5%) and 5-day returns is less than -0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A strong labor market (high PAYEMS growth) combined with robust consumer spending (high RSAFS) signals a healthy economic expansion that supports corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The Rank IC for the interaction term (PAYEMS * RSAFS) with 60-day SPX returns is less than 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansions (characterized by low but rising unemployment), the labor market tightness leads to wage pressures and potential inflation, causing the Fed to tighten policy and resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods meeting the trigger condition (UNRATE < 4.0% and 3mo change > 0.1pp), or the Rank IC for the trigger condition is less than -0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A higher level of housing starts (HOUST) indicates strong consumer confidence and economic activity, which supports corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The Rank IC between HOUST and 60-day SPX returns is less than 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 100 (relative to 2017=100) signals a weakening economy and potential recession, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO < 100, or the Rank IC between INDPRO and 5-day returns is greater than or equal to 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of high interest rates (FEDFUNDS > 4.0%) and high unemployment (UNRATE > 5.0%) signals a stagflationary environment, which is associated with negative equity returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods meeting the trigger condition (FEDFUNDS > 4.0% and UNRATE > 5.0%), or the Rank IC for the joint condition is less than -0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In the early stages of a post-recession recovery (INDPRO rising from below 95), industrial production growth signals improving economic conditions, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods meeting the trigger condition (INDPRO < 95 and 3mo change > 0.5pp), or the Rank IC for the trigger condition is less than 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
